term: Advanced chronic kidney disease (eGFR 25 or below, dialysis, or kidney transplant)
RENAL LIFECYCLE (University Medical Center Groningen lead; collaborators AstraZeneca and the Dutch Kidney Foundation; about 1,750 participants; dapagliflozin 10 mg/day against placebo) enrols 'Patients with advanced CKD i.e. an eGFR <=25 mL/min/1.73m2', 'Dialysis patients (at least 3 months after start of dialysis)' and 'Transplant patients with an eGFR <=45 mL/min/1.73m2'. Its primary outcome is the composite of all-cause mortality, kidney failure and hospitalisation for heart failure (registry, clinicaltrials.gov API v2, checked 2026-11-16). The Farxiga label (api.fda.gov set id 72ad22ae-efe6-4cd6-a302-98aaee423d69, effective 2026-06-03) approves CKD at risk of progression. But it says 'Initiation with FARXIGA is not recommended in patients with an eGFR less than 25 mL/min/1.73 m2' and 'Efficacy and safety trials with FARXIGA did not enroll patients with an eGFR less than 25 mL/min/1.73 m2 or on dialysis'. The study therefore enrols the part of CKD the label does not recommend starting in, and an approved-CKD link would read the readout as settled. label_covers is 'no' for initiation. The label lets a patient whose eGFR falls below 25 on treatment continue, so some prevalent users in the pool are already inside the revenue. MeSH has no concept for advanced CKD.
